facts.fact_text: On 30 October 1998, the applicant notified the Salzburg Federal Police Authority (Bundespolizeidirektion) under section 2 of the Assembly Act (Versammlungsgesetz) of a planned meeting.

The applicant notified the Salzburg Federal Police Authority that on All Saints' Day, 1 November 1998, from 9 a.m. until 1 p.m., he would be holding a meeting at the Salzburg municipal cemetery in front of the war memorial.
The applicant expected about six participants at the planned meeting.
The participants of the applicant's planned meeting would carry commemorative messages in their hands and attached to their clothes.
On 31 October 1998, the Salzburg Federal Police Authority prohibited the applicant's planned meeting.
The Salzburg Federal Police Authority relied on section 6 of the Assembly Act (Versammlungsgesetz) when prohibiting the applicant's planned meeting.
The Salzburg Federal Police Authority prohibited the applicant's planned meeting on the ground that it would endanger public order and security.
The Salzburg Federal Police Authority ordered that any remedies used against its decision to prohibit the applicant's planned meeting should not have suspensive effect.
As a result of the Salzburg Federal Police Authority's order that remedies should not have suspensive effect, the applicant's planned demonstration could not take place.

The Salzburg Federal Police Authority relied on Article 11 of the Convention when prohibiting the applicant's planned meeting.
The Assembly Act 1953 (Versammlungsgesetz) regulates the exercise of the right to freedom of assembly in Austria.
Pursuant to section 6 of the Assembly Act 1953 (Versammlungsgesetz), the competent authority must prohibit any assembly which would contravene criminal law or endanger public order and security.

In the years prior to 1999, a number of organisations had organised protest campaigns with the aim of disrupting the Comradeship IV (Kameradschaft IV) commemoration ceremony.
